newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-RJB sees bright future in coal.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-RJB sees bright future in coal.

text.p: RJB Mining Plc said on Tuesday it was confident the British coal industry would survive its battle with gas as the energy source for power generators.
The so-called "dash for gas" is still hurting coal sales, but RJB's chief executive Richard Budge believes the power generators will realise it is unwise to become overdependent on gas.
In 1990, about 80 percent of Britain's energy was generated by coal compared with 49 percent last year.

In an interview with Reuters, Budge said coal demand in the long-term would be underpinned be a wide recognition that it is undesirable for Britain to import large amounts of energy for power generation in the next century.
RJB sells a significant part of its production to electricity generators PowerGen Plc and National Power under long-term contracts, but these expire in 1998.
But there is a future for RJB beyond next year, Budge said.

"It (coal) is our only sustainable long-term energy source with decades of coal available at competitive prices, whereas more and more gas in the next century will be coming from Algeria and Russia," Budge said.
"Without a mixed portfolio we will be held ransom by gas in the future," he added after RJB earlier reported a 9.3 percent rise in 1996 pre-tax profit.
But coal sales fell to 37.6 milllion tonnes from 41.9 million due to gas competition. Budge, however, said the sales reduction was less than many industry watchers had expected.
Britain's coal market totalled 63 million tonnes last year while many forecast were for less than 50 million, he added.
"Everybody forecast by now that the coal industry was decimated, but in actual fact it is very alive and well," he said.
Budge said sales so far this year had been satisfactory, but he declined to elaborate.
